sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Tagged constructs were used in functional studies of inhibitory synapse formation (PMC3678166); surface expression of the Myc-tagged protein was confirmed by immunostaining of non-permeabilized cells, and the EGFP-tagged construct was used to visualize IgSF9b at synapses. Both tags were tolerated for surface trafficking and synaptic localization.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the tag was inserted 'between residues 28 and 29 of IgSF9b' in the full-length, membrane-anchored protein, making this a validated exact-site insertion. Python lookup confirms residues[28]='E' and residues[29]='E' in the canonical sequence; the junction is 8 residues into the mature ectodomain (SP cleavage after residue 20), well within the extracellular span (21-726) and 699 residues from the TM helix (727-744). Both a short epitope tag (Myc, 10 aa) and a large globular domain (EGFP, ~239 aa) were tolerated, strongly supporting steric permissiveness for a ~13-23 aa ALFA-type tag. Full-length membrane-anchored IgSF9b expressed in mammalian cells (pGW1 / pEGFP-N1 vectors); a Myc epitope (EQKLISEEDL, 10 aa) and, in a separate construct, EGFP (~239 aa) were each inserted between residues 28 and 29 of the full-length protein. Residue 28 lies 8 positions C-terminal to the signal-peptide cleavage site (SP: 1-20, mature N-terminus: 21), placing the junction squarely in the extracellular N-terminal region and 699 residues from the TM boundary (727). Python verification: residues[28]='E', residues[29]='E'; both positions confirmed extracellular.

sources.claim: Myc epitope (EQKLISEEDL) and EGFP was inserted between residues 28 and 29 of IgSF9b in pGW1 and pEGFP-N1, respectively.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It unambiguously pins a single site at junction 28|29 in the extracellular N-terminal region of full-length IGSF9B. No other insertions, loop-level precedents, or terminal tags are described in the ledger. The large extracellular domain (21-726) contains multiple Ig-like domains that could in principle accommodate tags in inter-domain linkers, but no ledger evidence supports any other specific position, so no additional sites are proposed. The intracellular tail (745-1349) is extensive but no snorkel or cytoplasmic tag is reported in the ledger.
